gaps.name: Sign-up screen for brand new accounts
gaps.whatItIs: AuthorizationSequenceSignUpController: after the code is accepted for a phone number that has no account, Telegram asks for first name, last name and an optional avatar, showing the terms of service (as a must-accept popup when showPopup is set, with a minimum-age confirmation).
gaps.whyItMatters: Right now a new user is permanently stuck. TGClient maps authorizationStateWaitRegistration to TGAuthStateWaitRegistration, but AppDelegate's onAuthState switch falls into `default: break`, so the code screen just freezes with no error. Only existing accounts can log in.
gaps.whereItGoes: New TGLoginStepRegistration in src/TGLoginViewController.m (two text fields reusing the existing input chrome, terms shown via TGAlertView), plus a case in the switch at src/AppDelegate.m:105.
tdlib: setProfilePhoto for the optional avatar - already wrapped in TGClient+Account

gaps.name: Auth state machine ignores the email, other-device and premium-purchase states
gaps.whatItIs: Modern AuthorizationSequenceController drives every screen off the authorization state, including authorizationStateWaitEmailAddress, WaitEmailCode, WaitOtherDeviceConfirmation and WaitPremiumPurchase.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGClient.m -handleAuthState: returns early on any state it does not recognise (the `else { return; }` at line 426), so those four never reach the UI. Our email and QR steps only appear when the user taps a button; when the server pushes an email second factor after the code, or when the QR is scanned on the other device, the screen does not move. The login email flow is fully wrapped but effectively unreachable in the server-driven direction.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGClient.h TGAuthState enum, src/TGClient.m:403 -handleAuthState:, and the switch in src/AppDelegate.m:105 routing to the existing showEmailStep/showEmailCodeStep/showQrStep methods in TGLoginViewController.m.
tdlib: authorizationStateWaitEmailAddress / WaitEmailCode / WaitOtherDeviceConfirmation - parsing only; setAuthenticationEmailAddress, checkAuthenticationEmailCode and requestQrCodeLogin are already wrapped (TGClient+Account.h)

gaps.name: Word and phrase login codes are untypable
gaps.whatItIs: TDLib now issues authenticationCodeTypeSmsWord and SmsPhrase, where the login code is a word or a short phrase (with a first_letter hint), not digits. Modern's code entry switches to a text field for those cases.
gaps.whyItMatters: showCodeStepWithPhoneNumber hardcodes UIKeyboardTypeNumberPad (TGLoginViewController.m:733) and the length check expects digits, so on any account Telegram routes to a word code, the user physically cannot enter it and login is dead. TGAccountCodeDescription already recognises the two type names but tells the user it sent 'an SMS with the code'.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGLoginViewController.m -showCodeStepWithPhoneNumber:/-applyCodeInfo:, keyed off the existing "type" field; wording in TGAccountCodeDescription at src/TGClient+Account.m:55.
tdlib: authenticationCodeTypeSmsWord / SmsPhrase first_letter - already parsed in TGClient+Account.m, just not surfaced in the info dictionary

gaps.name: Account reset when the 2FA password is lost
gaps.whatItIs: AuthorizationSequenceAwaitingAccountResetController: when the user has a cloud password but no working recovery email, Telegram offers to delete and reset the account after a waiting period, showing a live countdown until the reset can be confirmed.
gaps.whyItMatters: The password step offers only 'Forgot password?', which mails a recovery code. A user with no recovery email hits a dead end and can never get back into their number, which is the exact situation this screen exists for.
gaps.whereItGoes: New branch off TGLoginStepPassword in src/TGLoginViewController.m (the recovery path around line 783 already exists), reusing the countdown timer machinery already there for resend.
tdlib: deleteAccount - wrapped as -deleteAccountWithReason:password:completion: (TGClient+Privacy.h:182); it also works in authorizationStateWaitPassword and returns the pending wait period in the error text

gaps.name: Authorising another device by scanning its QR code
gaps.whatItIs: Scanning a tg://login?token= QR shown by a desktop or web client, then confirming a sheet that names the device, app, IP and location before granting the session.
gaps.whyItMatters: This is the only way to sign in to Telegram Desktop or Web from this phone, and it is half-built: -confirmQrCodeLogin: is wrapped in TGClient+Account.m:401 with no caller anywhere in src. TGQRViewController recognises the 'login' path component (line 332) but then just prints the URL as text, so the scan silently does nothing useful.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGQRViewController.m, the tg:// handling near line 332 - call -confirmQrCodeLogin: and present the returned session dictionary in a TGActionSheet before confirming.

gaps.name: Unconfirmed new-login banner
gaps.whatItIs: When a new session signs in, modern Telegram puts a banner at the top of the chat list, 'New login from <device>', with Confirm and Terminate actions, so a stolen SMS code can be caught within the grace window.
gaps.whyItMatters: -unconfirmedSessionsWithCompletion: exists (TGClient+Privacy.h:77) and has no caller outside the Sessions screen; the isUnconfirmed flag is parsed in two places and shown nowhere prominent. Without the banner the user only learns of an intrusion if they happen to open Settings, Sessions.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGChatListViewController.m as a header view above the list, actions calling the already-wrapped -confirmSession: and -terminateSession:.
tdlib: getActiveSessions / confirmSession / terminateSession - all wrapped in TGClient+Privacy.h
updateUnconfirmedSession - needs an update hook in TGClient.m

gaps.name: Multiple accounts on one device
gaps.whatItIs: Modern Telegram keeps several logged-in accounts side by side, switchable from the settings header, with per-account unread badges and notifications, and an Add Account entry that re-enters the login sequence without logging the current account out.
gaps.whyItMatters: Anyone with a personal and a work number has to log out and back in, re-entering an SMS code every switch, and loses the local database each time. It is the single largest structural gap in this area.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGClient is a singleton around one td_json_client (src/TGClient.m); this needs a client-per-account registry, per-account TDLib database directories, and a switcher row in src/TGSettingsViewController.m. Telegraph at /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/twelve/Telegraph/ predates multi-account and offers no help here.
tdlib: td_json_client_create per account, plus routing every existing request/update path through the active client - none of this is wrapped; TGClient assumes one instance throughout
